name: ORCA-Fusion BT (C15440-20UP)

specs.Read noise: 0.7 e- rms (ultra-quiet scan); 1.6 e- rms (fast scan)
specs.Cooling: -8 °C (air or water); below -15 °C at maximum water cooling

summary: Back-thinned sCMOS camera with a 5.3-megapixel sensor of 6.5 µm pixels and three readout modes that trade speed against read noise. Its quietest mode brings read noise below 1 electron.

sources.title: Hamamatsu ORCA-Fusion BT C15440-20UP product page

name: ORCA-Quest 2 (C15550-22UP)

specs.Read noise: 0.30 e- rms (ultra-quiet scan); 0.43 e- rms (standard scan)
specs.Cooling: -20 °C (air or water); -35 °C at maximum water cooling

summary: Quantitative CMOS (qCMOS) camera with deep sub-electron read noise, down to 0.30 electrons rms. It combines a 9.4-megapixel sensor of small 4.6 µm pixels with deep cooling for very low dark current.

sources.title: Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 C15550-22UP product page

name: ORCA-Flash4.0 V3 (C13440-20CU)

specs.Read noise: 1.4 e- rms (slow scan); 1.6 e- rms (standard scan)
specs.Max frame rate: 100 fps full frame (Camera Link); 40 fps (USB 3.0, 16 bit)

summary: Four-megapixel sCMOS camera with 6.5 µm pixels and about 1.5 electrons rms read noise. It reaches 100 full frames per second over Camera Link, or 40 fps over USB 3.0.

sources.title: Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V3 C13440-20CU product page

name: ORCA-Lightning (C14120-20P)

specs.Read noise: 2.0 e- rms (standard full-well mode); 2.7 e- rms (high full-well mode)

summary: Large-format 12-megapixel sCMOS camera with an F-mount and a CoaXPress interface, built for high-throughput imaging such as light-sheet microscopy. It reads four sensor lines at once to reach 121 full frames per second.

sources.title: Hamamatsu ORCA-Lightning C14120-20P brochure (SCAS0132E, distributor copy)

name: Prime BSI Express
summary: Back-illuminated sCMOS camera built on the GPixel GSense2020BSI sensor, combining 95% peak QE with 6.5 µm pixels and 1 electron read noise. It connects over USB 3.2.

sources.title: Teledyne Vision Solutions: Prime BSI Express

name: Prime BSI
summary: Back-illuminated sCMOS camera using the GPixel GSense2020BSI sensor with 6.5 µm pixels and about 1 electron median read noise. It is offered with PCIe or USB 3.0 interfaces.

sources.title: Teledyne Vision Solutions: Prime BSI

name: Prime 95B
summary: Back-illuminated sCMOS camera with large 11 µm pixels on the GPixel GSense400BSI sensor, aimed at low-light work where light collection per pixel matters more than pixel count. Larger 22 mm and 25 mm sensor versions are also listed.

sources.title: Teledyne Vision Solutions: Prime 95B

name: Kinetix

specs.Pixels: 10.2 MP (20.8 x 20.8 mm sensor, 29.4 mm diagonal)
specs.Read noise: 0.7 e- (16-bit sub-electron mode); 1.2 e- (12-bit sensitivity mode)

summary: Back-illuminated sCMOS camera that reads a 10-megapixel, 29.4 mm diagonal sensor at about 500 frames per second. Selectable modes trade speed for read noise down to 0.7 electrons.

sources.title: Teledyne Vision Solutions: Kinetix

name: Evolve 512 Delta

specs.Read noise: <1 e- with EM gain; 75 e- at 20 MHz without EM gain

summary: Back-thinned 512 x 512 EMCCD camera whose electron-multiplying gain lifts single-photon signals above the read noise. It was marketed for single-molecule and super-resolution imaging, with a LightSpeed mode for fast region-of-interest readout.

sources.title: Photometrics Evolve 512 Delta datasheet, Rev A10 (2015), distributor copy

name: Cascade 128+

specs.Read noise: <65 e- rms at 12 MHz; <1 e- rms with EM gain

summary: Early back-illuminated frame-transfer EMCCD camera with a small 128 x 128 array of large pixels, chosen for speed in neuroscience and single-molecule fluorescence. It records more than 500 full 16-bit frames per second.

sources.title: Photometrics Cascade 128+ datasheet, PM-DS-002 Rev C1 (2010)

name: iXon Ultra 888
summary: Back-illuminated megapixel EMCCD with single-photon sensitivity over a 13.3 mm square sensor. Its 30 MHz readout and crop mode give higher frame rates from sub-regions, such as 93 fps for 512 x 512.

sources.title: Andor iXon Ultra EMCCD specifications

name: iXon Ultra 897
summary: Back-illuminated 512 x 512 EMCCD with 16 µm pixels, overclocked to 56 full frames per second while keeping single-photon sensitivity. Andor lists single-molecule detection and super-resolution among its key applications.

sources.title: Andor iXon Ultra EMCCD specifications

name: Sona 4.2B-11
summary: Vacuum-cooled back-illuminated sCMOS camera whose 11 µm pixels cover a 32 mm diagonal, a very large field for a microscope camera. A 6.5 µm-pixel Sona-6 variant trades field size for speed (up to 135 fps).

sources.title: Andor Sona sCMOS brochure and specifications

name: Zyla 4.2 PLUS
summary: Compact, thermoelectrically cooled sCMOS camera with 6.5 µm pixels, 82% peak QE and sub-electron read noise. A dual-gain sensor design gives a dynamic range of about 33,000:1.

sources.title: Andor Zyla 5.5 and 4.2 PLUS specifications

name: Marana 4.2B-11
summary: Vacuum-cooled back-illuminated sCMOS camera aimed mainly at astronomy and physical sciences, with a 32 mm diagonal sensor of 11 µm pixels. A 6.5 µm-pixel Marana 4.2B-6 model reaches 135 fps.

sources.title: Andor Marana sCMOS specifications

name: pco.edge 4.2 bi USB

specs.Read noise: 1.9 e- rms (standard mode); 1.1 e- rms (low-light mode)

summary: Deep-cooled back-illuminated sCMOS camera with a 4.2-megapixel sensor of 6.5 µm pixels and a USB 3.1 interface. A UV variant extends the spectral range down to 190 nm.

sources.title: pco.edge 4.2 bi (UV) USB datasheet v2.0.0

name: Retiga E7
summary: Cooled CMOS camera with very low dark current, designed to allow exposures of up to 60 minutes as well as routine fluorescence imaging.

sources.title: Teledyne Vision Solutions: Retiga E

name: SPAD512

specs.Max frame rate: 100,000 fps at 1 bit (buffered); 400 fps at 8 bit continuous

summary: Single-photon avalanche diode camera that counts photons with no read noise and a global shutter. On-chip time gating, down to 6 ns gates shifted in 17 ps steps, supports widefield fluorescence lifetime imaging.

sources.title: Pi Imaging SPAD512 datasheet (Quantum Design copy)

name: Power HyD S
summary: Silicon multi-pixel photon counter (MPPC) detector at the core of Leica STELLARIS confocals, working in analog or photon-counting mode. Leica reports more than double the dynamic range of classical photon counting by resolving overlapping photon pulses.

sources.title: Leica Microsystems: The Power HyD detector family
The Power HyD family of detectors for confocal microscopy (Nature Methods application note, Oct 2020)

name: Power HyD X

specs.Detector: GaAsP photocathode coupled to an avalanche diode

summary: Actively cooled GaAsP hybrid detector for STELLARIS systems, tuned for fast lifetime imaging, FCS and single-molecule work. It gives accurate photon arrival times with negligible afterpulsing.

sources.title: Leica Microsystems: The Power HyD detector family
The Power HyD family of detectors for confocal microscopy (Nature Methods application note, Oct 2020)

name: Power HyD R

specs.Detector: extended-red GaAsP photocathode coupled to an avalanche diode

summary: Cooled hybrid detector with an extended-red GaAsP photocathode for near-infrared fluorophores on STELLARIS 8, with detection up to 850 nm. It also supports photon counting and lifetime measurements.

sources.title: Leica Microsystems: The Power HyD detector family
The Power HyD family of detectors for confocal microscopy (Nature Methods application note, Oct 2020)

name: Airyscan detector
summary: Area detector on ZEISS LSM confocals that splits the pinhole plane into 32 elements, each acting as a very small pinhole. Together they work as one large detector, so more light is collected than through a single small pinhole.

sources.title: ZEISS LSM 990 product page

name: 32-channel GaAsP spectral detector

specs.Channels: 32 GaAsP channels; up to 36 channels in total with side detectors
specs.Spectral range: 380-900 nm in a single scan (full system)

summary: Multichannel GaAsP spectral detector in ZEISS LSM confocals that records many emission bands at once for spectral imaging and unmixing. On the LSM 990 it is combined with side detectors and optional near-infrared GaAs/GaAsP detectors.

sources.title: ZEISS LSM 990 product page

name: H7422P-40
summary: Photosensor module that combines a cooled GaAsP-photocathode photomultiplier tube with its own high-voltage supply. The P version has high gain for photon counting.

sources.title: Hamamatsu H7422 series photosensor module datasheet

name: SPCM-AQRH
summary: Single-channel module built on a cooled silicon avalanche photodiode that outputs one TTL pulse per detected photon from 400 to 1060 nm. Models are graded by dark count rate and dead time.

sources.title: Excelitas SPCM-AQRH datasheet, Rev 2023-1

name: Falcon 4i

specs.DQE: 0.92 at zero frequency, 0.50 at Nyquist (300 kV, EER)

summary: Direct electron detector for cryo-EM that counts individual electrons and can save them event by event in the Electron Event Representation (EER) format. It also has a fast linear survey mode.

sources.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific Falcon 4i direct electron detector

name: DE-64
summary: Large-format direct detection camera for transmission electron microscopes with an 8k x 8k sensor, aimed at cryo-EM of large specimens and cellular tomography. Single-electron counting is available as an option.

sources.title: Direct Electron DE-64

name: Apollo
summary: Event-based counting detector for cryo-EM that finds and centroids each electron event in FPGA hardware. It is designed for single-particle analysis, cryo-electron tomography and MicroED at high dose rates.

sources.title: Direct Electron Apollo

name: K3
summary: Electron-counting direct detection camera for cryo-EM and low-dose TEM; a larger, faster successor to the K2 with a 1.6x larger field of view.

sources.title: Gatan: K3 camera
Microscopy and Microanalysis (2018): K3, a first look
Northwestern NUANCE: Gatan K3 (pixel size)
